Should a runningback like Murray who ran really well behind top lines be viewed as less than a RB like Lynch who ran behind a poor O-line?

Funny thing about Murray, he didn't always have a good offensive line. 2011 we had Tyron Smith, who was also a rookie, and Doug Free. Aside from that there were turnstiles. Murray averaged 5.5 ypc that year. Murray is good in his own right, but he tends to break down as the season goes on. In 2014, Murray averaged 5.14 ypc in the first ten games. In the following six games, he averaged 4.1 ypc. In the last three games of the regular season, it was only 3.42 ypc. So Murray, like Lynch, is still plenty good without the offensive line, but he just isn't nearly as durable. Lynch has had over 200 carries every season but one he's been in the league. Murray has had over 200 carries only half of the seasons he's been in the league, which is two.

So yeah, Lynch is a better back than Murray because he can keep it up longer. Put Lynch behind the Cowboys offensive line, and I bet he makes a run at Dickerson's record, because he'll be able to keep having games averaging 5 ypc late into the season.
